meta.title: The kinds-of-numbers inventory: what is already measured
meta.scope: desk only; no card was touched; every number is read from a committed file or typed from a committed README with its citation
meta.repo_head_note: run `git log -1` for the head this was built at

normalisation.mac_vs_flop: 1 multiply-add = 2 flops. MAC/s = TFLOPS x 1e12 / 2. One 16x16x16 TensorFMA = 4096 multiply-adds, so MAC/s = ops/s x 4096.
normalisation.cycles_per_op: fp32 546, fp16 546, int8 318 (tools/claims-v3/hpl/surface_hpl.py; measured identical on three cards to 0.0002 cycle, claims-v3 ABLB-2a). int8 is therefore 6.9x fp32's MAC rate at the same clock, not 4x.
normalisation.clock_600_vs_800: NEVER scale a price by the clock ratio. E72 ran ONE card at both: 79.18 +- 3.09 fJ at 600 MHz / 0.5179 V against 121.27 +- 0.61 fJ at 800 MHz / 0.6174 V - the price follows the VOLTAGE, 10-15% below a pure V^2 extrapolation, exponent bracketed 1.60-2.92, and the clock-scaling rival n = 3.637 excluded at >= 3.4 SE. E64's own governor model uses (V/0.517)^2 x f/600, i.e. s(700) = 1.408 and s(800) = 1.905 over s(600) = 1.0; cells marked `modelled` that cross clocks use exactly that factor and say so.
normalisation.card_to_card: at the SAME die temperature aifoundry3 switches 0.958-0.969 of aifoundry2 over the Horace patterns (E38's post-data note C2; E46's independent catalogue 0.972), and a2's 600 MHz per-bit price is 0.970 of a3's (E72). A cross-card quote carries about 3%. aifoundry1 card 1 idled at 50.15 W against a2's 36.34 and a3's 25.78 in September and borrows a2's leakage slope.
normalisation.baseline: THREE different zeros are in play and they are not interchangeable. (a) OVER IDLE: claims-v3 `switching` (board minus pre-launch idle minus leakage x the rise since launch), the September p_early - p_before, and E64's model term c. (b) OVER ZEROS: E67's anchors differenced against anchor_zeros, and the E15 rail column - these subtract a RUNNING kernel on zero data, so they omit the 8.6 W of lane un-gating. (c) OVER A CONSTANT OPERAND: every bit price in table 2 (lq_h0, aq_h0, lb_h0) - a constant NON-zero operand, so the lane is un-gated and only the flips are missing. (b) and (c) differ by that 8.6 W; (a) and (c) differ by the whole zeros level. Each cell's `conditions` names its own baseline.
normalisation.leakage_slope: a leakage slope is NOT a card constant (E71): it rises about 0.009 W/C per C on aifoundry2 and 0.011 on aifoundry3 over 51-65 C. Measured idle slopes: a2 0.2936 over 51-58 C (E66) and 0.3452 over 58-62; a3 0.3200 over 52-58 and 0.3803 +- 0.0036 over 58-62 (E71). The September campaign used 0.81 (a2, at an 80.9 C launch) and 0.55 (a3, at 55.8 C), fitted then. E68's registered estimator used 1.508 W/C, which is 4-5x every measured idle slope and is a busy transient, not leakage - its prices are published at both footings and the measured one is the better. Re-pricing the a3 ladders at E71's slope moves prices a few per cent and systematically (E65's flat mantissa floor 109 -> ~103 fJ, bit 22 1008 -> 986, the flow-M flip 745 +- 56 -> 722 +- 61 fJ) and moves none of the 16 registered verdicts.
normalisation.launch_temperature: September a2 and a1c1 launched at 80.9 C and a3 at 55.8 C; E64 launched at 50-57 C; the bit ladders at 58 C. Switching power itself drifts with die temperature at +22.0 +- 36.1 mW/C (E65 D1, re-read as +32.4 +- 39.6 at E71's slope) - consistent with zero and UNDECIDED, so it is not corrected for anywhere; it is a stated uncertainty of about +-1%/10 C.
normalisation.toggles: quote `nets_hier`, not `nets` (Q126(b)). The 21 Sep figure of 21,331 net toggles per random fp32 multiply-add reproduces only under the Verilator it was measured with (5.042, a coverage-counter defect in two compressor modules) and was never a count of wires; the figure to quote is about 1,301 per multiply-add, 8-16x smaller.
normalisation.rail_vs_board: the minion rail carries 4.774 pJ [4.549-4.951] of the board's 5.783 pJ per random fp32 multiply-add, ratio 0.825 [0.787-0.856] (Q129). The 1.009 pJ between them is mostly the regulators' delivery loss (0.875 pJ), which is a named account, not a bottom-up row.

e65_flowM_fJ.note: b bit 11 alternating against a = pi, board, all-in; E71 re-prices it 722 +- 61 fJ

e68_lo12_fJ_band.note: sm_lo12 at the registered 1.508 W/C and at E66's measured 0.296 W/C; the band is the leakage slope, which E68 never measured on its own data

mechanisms.what_it_does: an all-zero operand word turns the lane's work off, so the die never sees the switching at all
mechanisms.size: 8.6 W of the zeros->random step at 600 MHz on aifoundry3, with 16.1 W of operand flips on top (24.66 W in all)
mechanisms.notes: the chip gates the all-zero BIT PATTERN only, so -0.0 is not gated: it costs +8.36 W over +0.0 and is indistinguishable from all-ones (claims-v3 abla ABL-T1). The VECTOR fmadd.ps has no zero gate at all (E61, 0.087 +- 0.060 W).

mechanisms.what_it_does: the SAME arithmetic costs more when consecutive operands differ in more bits, because the flips, not the values, are what is paid for
mechanisms.size: max-flip minus Gray on the same 4,096 multiply-adds: +0.682 +- 0.010 W (aifoundry3, 600 MHz, bits 0-3) and +1.291 +- 0.009 W (aifoundry2, 800 MHz); the four orders rank by their flipped bits, and binary is indistinguishable from Gray at bits 0-3
mechanisms.notes: this is the cleanest single demonstration for a blog reader: identical results, identical count of operations, different energy.

mechanisms.what_it_does: two flips that travel the same wires do not cost twice one flip, so a word's price is a saturating function of the additive sum of its bits' prices
mechanisms.size: one curve dW = Winf(1 - e^(-S/Winf)) fits 15 B-side rungs to 0.232 W rms against 1.358 W for any law in Hamming weight alone and 6.062 W for pure additivity; summing per-bit prices over a random word over-predicts by about 2x
mechanisms.notes: WHICH bits flip beats HOW MANY: 8 spread mantissa bits cost +3.860 +- 0.052 W more than the low 8 at the same Hamming weight (73.9 SE). Winf is the curve's CURVATURE, not a ceiling - correction C1 withdrew the ceiling reading.

mechanisms.what_it_does: a high mantissa bit drives a wider slice of the multiplier tree than a low one, so the same single flip costs 12x more at bit 22 than at bit 6
mechanisms.size: B side 83 fJ (bit 6) to 1,008 fJ (bit 22), span 12.2x; A side 153 fJ (bit 4) to 1,440 fJ (bit 22), span 9.4x; exponent bits average 174 (B) / 265 (A) fJ and the sign bit 123 / 247 fJ
mechanisms.notes: the mantissa is TWO regimes: bits 0-9 flat at ~109 fJ, then a monotone climb from bit 10. 'The exponent is dearer than the low mantissa' holds only below bit 10 (E65 A3 and E67 P3 both FAIL on that clause).

mechanisms.what_it_does: a flipped bit costs more when the OTHER operand is a busy number, because the partial products it selects are themselves wide
mechanisms.size: A = pi over A = 1.0 is 1.59-4.73x at the five shared B positions (5 of 5 at >= 2 SE); B = pi over B = 1.0 reaches 1,566 fJ at A bit 22. On the ladder SLOPE the effect is only +11% (116.7 -> 129.9 fJ)
mechanisms.notes: the two operands' flow-M prices agree within 30% (B 745, A 856 fJ), and the two operand PATHS add (0.88 of the sum) even though bits within one operand do not.

mechanisms.what_it_does: a flip's price follows the rail voltage the governor picks, not the clock it picks with it
mechanisms.size: the same card reads 79.18 +- 3.09 fJ at 600 MHz / 0.5179 V and 121.27 +- 0.61 fJ at 800 MHz / 0.6174 V; the board price is 10-15% below a pure V^2 extrapolation, the exponent is bracketed 1.60-2.92, and the clock-scaling rival n = 3.637 is excluded at >= 3.4 SE in every reduction
mechanisms.notes: quote E72 as 'the price follows the voltage, not the clock', never as 'the exponent is 2'.

mechanisms.what_it_does: on the DRAM path what costs is the NUMBER OF ONES in flight, not the number of bits that changed
mechanisms.size: 3.255 pJ per carried one at DRAM [2.97, 3.55] against nothing measurable at L1 (-0.0001 pJ); 94% of the 1,008 pJ per 64 B line the two counts explain is the ones term
mechanisms.notes: so off chip, PACKING ZEROS is the big lever and reducing transitions the small one - the opposite of the arithmetic path. DRAM's changed-bit arm is unresolved (non-monotone in every pass): quote a bound.

mechanisms.mechanism: the governor (power test, then thermal test)
mechanisms.what_it_does: the watts the data causes are turned into SPEED by the firmware, which regulates a ~1.3 s average of board power to the TDP and the die reading to the threshold
mechanisms.size: on a cool die the power test alone acts, so zeros run 12.3 against random fp32's 10.7 TFLOPS in the first 8 s (15%); in 80 s runs the thermal test wins, because this card's cooling puts the die at 65 C at about 50 W, and zeros run 12.3 against 9.2 TFLOPS (33%)
mechanisms.notes: the model is a first-order average, tau 1.3 s, compared once per 0.24 s pass, one step up or down, 3.3 MHz rms over 26 cool-die runs; the thermal line is die = 41.88 + 0.4696 C per board W. E69 moved the cap for the first time and 12 of 12 extrapolated cap-table cells held.
